newsitem.title: UK: Queens Moat sells 25 British hotels.
newsitem.headline: Queens Moat sells 25 British hotels.

text.p: British hotels group Queens Moat Houses Plc has sold 25 hotels for 91.5 million pounds ($150.1 million) as a single portfolio to a management buy-in group.

Britain's Queens Moat Houses (QMH) said in a statement it had sold the 19 County Hotels and six Moat Houses to a buy-in group formed by Hambro European Ventures Limited, the venture capital arm of British merchant bank Hambros Plc.

QMH said approximately 91.5 million pounds would be "cash payable on completion". It said a further one million pounds "may be receivable in the event of a subsequent flotation or sale (of the hotels)".

The hotels group has been implementing a recovery strategy since the end of 1993 to rationalise its hotel portfolio and meet its debts. It said the sale of the hotels had substantially reduced its debt repayment burden for 1997 and 1998.
"This disposal represents an important step in the group's recovery. It achieves almost the whole of the group's UK disposal programme in a single step," QMH's chief executive Andrew Coppel said.

QMH has sold 28 hotels individually since November 1993 "realising net proceeds of some 48 million pounds". It said the sale of the 25 hotels meant it was nearing completion of its British disposal programme with one other hotel, Billesley Manor, currently for sale and being marketed separately.
The group said it would repay its lending banks approximately 71.5 million pounds early and retain the balance of the net sale proceeds of 17.5 million pounds "principally for reinvestment".

QMH said it considers "prospects for further profits growth remain sound", adding that in the second half of 1996 it had continued to make satisfactory trading process and had benefited from lower interest rates on its bank debt.

"The board is encouraged by the development of the group's profitability and in particular by the performances in the UK and the Netherlands," it said, adding that it was cautiously optimistic about the medium term prospects for the German hotel market place.

It said that it had taken action in France and Belgium "to stabilise certain under-performing hotels and to inject capital expenditure selectively, pending a modest anticipated recovery in coming years".
